p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of the role of voltage-gated and ligand-gated ion channels in neural transmission. Diagram of the role of voltage-gated and ligand-gated ion channels in neural transmission. The diagram shows the axon of the presynaptic neuron, represented by a structure that resembles an open test-tube. This structure appears to be sitting on top of another text-tube structure, except this one is upside down - this represents the cell body of a postsynaptic neuron. There are six phases depicted in the diagram. In the axon of the presynpatic neuron, to the left side of the tube, there are seven blue plus signs, one on top of the other, complemented by seven pink minus signs on the inside. There is a blue arrow on the left side of the neuron, and 3 plus charges appear to be coming in through the Na plus channel. This represents depolarization. Right below are two small red buttons, labeled "Voltage-gated Na plus channel" and two small purple buttons, labeled "Voltage-gated Ca2 plus." The right side of the tube is lined with small green buttons, which are labeled "Voltage-gated K plus channel." Theres's a red arrow pointing downward inside the right side of the tube, marked with three white plus charges. Two of the plus charges are leaving the neuron, indicated by an arrow passing through the K plus channels. This represents repolarization of the cell. In between the red and purple buttons described before are minus charges, with the exception of the charge between the third and fourth buttons, which is a plus sign. Below the second Ca2 plus channel, there are four plus charges, complemented by four minus charges on the inside of the tube. At the bottom of the axon are eight secretory vesicles containing acetylcholine; these vesicles are represented as small blue and yellow ringed structures with red pellets inside. Two of the vesicles appear open, allowing acetylcholine (the red pellets) to flow out past the synaptic cleft (represented as a blue section between the axon of the presynaptic neuron and the cell body of the postsynaptic neuron). Acetylcholine then binds to two green structures, which are receptors in the cell body. In the cell body, there are two curved arrows pointing downward, a blue on the left and a red one on the right. Two Na plus are entering the cell, as indicated by arrows passing through the red buttons - below them, there is one blue plus sign, and then below that, there are four additional blue plus signs on the outside, complemented by four pink minus signs on the inside. On the opposite side is the red arrow, which is marked with two white plus signs. A K plus seems to be leaving the cell through one of the three green buttons. Below the second and third green buttons, there are pink minus signs on the inside complementing two blue plus signs on the outside. This section is labeled "Action Potential."
